attribution_limitations: The abstract says the probable abdominal ectopic pregnancy was confirmed by MRI, but the case text says MRI showed a left adnexal EP presumed to be within the fallopian tube, the discussion says the MRI report of a tubal ectopic pregnancy did not correlate with surgical findings, and histology confirmed a para-ovarian abdominal ectopic pregnancy.
The case text cites Figure 2C,D for the repeat ultrasound, but Figure 2 is the combined screening test and the Figure 1 caption labels panels C and D as the second ultrasound.

The Figure 1 caption gives nuchal translucency 3.1 mm (and the Figure 1B image prints NT 3.1mm), while the image-only Figure 2 table prints NT 31.0 mm. This is treated as a decimal-place print artefact in pixel content; pixel values are never a conflict side, so the caption fact stays included with this ambiguity.

Figure 2 (image-only table) prints PAPP-A corrected MoM 0.06 with a truncation note, matching the text 0.06 MoM; it also prints a screening b-hCG of 88.00 IU/L, which differs from the Table 1 BhCG of 119,656 IU/L, and an individual trisomy 21 chance of >1 in 2 where the text says 1 in 2. The source does not make the screening b-hCG and the Table 1 BhCG the same measurement or time point, so there is no conflict; the >1 in 2 versus 1 in 2 difference is precision-level. Image values are pixel content only and the text/table facts stay included.
The case text names the handheld device as GE Voluson Air, while the competing-interests statement names a loaned Vscan Air device.
The source reports both an adnexectomy and a left salpingo-oophorectomy without stating whether they are the same operation.
Cessation of cord pulsation is described, but fetal death, termination or stillbirth is not literally stated.
The table lists blood results without collection times or flags, and the text does not time them relative to imaging or surgery.

The MRI is described as "Same-day" without naming the event it shares a day with, and no sentence orders the MRI, repeat ultrasound, handheld ultrasound or Table 1 blood tests against each other or against surgery.
